# Audit Question Finder {#sec-finder}

Start here when you have an audit question and want to know where the book answers it. The questions are grouped by audit area. Each row names the technique and the section that shows it at work. Links with a small arrow leave this book. Here they open the companion book, *Applied Audit Analytics with R*, where the technique is applied to a whole audit area.

Type a word in the box to narrow the list, for example *duplicate*, *vendor*, *pension* or *map*.

```{=html}
<div class="finder-search">
  <input type="search" id="finder-filter" placeholder="Filter the questions" aria-label="Filter the audit questions">
  <span id="finder-count" aria-live="polite"></span>
</div>
```

::: {#finder}

## Accounts and journal entries {.unnumbered}

| Audit question | Technique | Where |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Is the ledger extract I received complete? | Balance check, reconciling to the trial balance, gaps in entry numbers | [Section 1.4](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-complete) |
| Which entries were recorded after the books were closed? | Entry time stamp against posting date | [Section 1.6.1](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-late) |
| Who is posting journal entries who should not be? | User master, segregation of duties | [Section 1.6.2](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-users), [Section 1.10](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-user) |
| Which entries were made at night, at weekends or on holidays? | Hour, day of the week and a holiday list | [Section 1.6.3](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-hours) |
| Were any entries approved by the person who made them? | Maker against approver | [Section 1.6.4](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-self) |
| Is someone keeping entries just below an approval limit? | A band below the limit, counted by user | [Section 1.6.5](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-limit) |
| Do the amounts of manual entries follow Benford's Law, and whose entries do not? | First-two digits, overall and by user | [Section 1.6.7](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-benford) |
| Which entries were posted twice, or reversed soon after the year end? | Matching entry signatures | [Section 1.6.9](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-dup), [Section 1.6.10](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-reversed) |
| Which accounts are combined in unusual ways? | Counting debit and credit account pairs | [Section 1.7](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-pairs) |
| Was revenue boosted at the year end? | Post-closing entries to revenue, followed to their reversal | [Section 1.9](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-revenue) |
| How do I choose which journal entries to examine? | A weighted risk score plus a random sample | [Section 1.8](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-score), [Section 1.8.1](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22-journal-entries.html#sec-jet-select) |
| Do the cash book and the bank statement agree, and what explains the difference? | Step-by-step matching with exact, tolerance and window joins | [Section 2.3](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-steps), [Section 2.4.3](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-statement) |
| How do I match records that have no common key or are written differently? | Cleaned references, inequality joins, string distance | [Section 2.3.1](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-prepare), [Section 2.3.3](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-window), [Section 2.3.6](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-fuzzy) |
| Does one bank credit settle several bills? | Small combinations within a party and a date window | [Section 2.3.5](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-combn) |
| Which reconciling items are old, stale or permanent? | Classifying and ageing what is left | [Section 2.4.1](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-left) |
| Did the unpresented cheques and deposits in transit really clear? | Matching against the next month's statement | [Section 2.4.2](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-subsequent) |
| Is a difference a transposition error? | A difference divisible by 9 | [Section 2.3.7](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-transpose) |
| Was input tax credit claimed on invoices the suppliers never reported? | Purchase register against GSTR-2B, invoice by invoice | [Section 2.5](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-itc) |
| Do the department's figures agree with the treasury's? | Totals by month and head, compared | [Section 2.6](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22b-reconciliation.html#sec-recon-treasury) |

| Which vendors were paid soon after registration, or woke up after years? | Days from creation to first payment, and earlier years' payments | [Section 6.4.1](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22c-payables.html#sec-pay-newvendor), [Section 6.4.2](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22c-payables.html#sec-pay-dormant) |

| Are vendor PANs and GSTINs valid, and do unregistered vendors get large payments? | Format and check digit, and totals of vendors with no GSTIN | [Section 6.4.6](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22c-payables.html#sec-pay-ids), [Section 6.4.7](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22c-payables.html#sec-pay-nogstin) |

| Were goods paid for before they arrived, or paid in full when only part arrived? | Payment against receipt dates, and value received | [Section 6.5.5](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22c-payables.html#sec-pay-before), [Section 6.5.6](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22c-payables.html#sec-pay-part) |

| Which vendors should I examine first? | A count of flags per vendor | [Section 6.8](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/22c-payables.html#sec-pay-risk) |
| Was the same bill paid twice? | Exact and near duplicates | @sec-dup-exact, @sec-dup-ssd |
| Were duplicates hidden by spaces, case or spelling? | Cleaning before matching | @sec-dup-hidden, @sec-strng-names |
| Are amounts kept just below a sanction limit? | Charts, Nigrini's tests | @sec-baseplot-audit, @sec-ggplot2-split, @sec-nigrini |
| Were payments made beyond the sanctioned amount? | Filtering and summarising | @sec-dplyr-audit |
| Was the rate in force on the date of the bill applied? | Rolling joins | @sec-joins-audit |
| Is one bill of a vendor far larger than its other bills? | Relative size factor | @sec-nigrini-rsf |
| Are there too many round amounts? | Round number test | @sec-nigrini-round |
| Does the same amount occur far too often? | Number duplication test | @sec-nigrini-numdup |
| Do the amounts look made up? | Benford's Law | @sec-benford, @sec-benford-offices |
| Are any cheque or voucher numbers missing? | Gaps in sequences | @sec-gaps-cheque |

| Are some firms taking turns to win our works tenders? | Repeated line-ups, a reshuffling test of the order of wins | [Section 4.5](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-bid-rigging.html#sec-bidrig-cobid), [Section 4.6](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-bid-rigging.html#sec-bidrig-rotation) |
| Do losing bids sit a steady margin above the winner? | Cover margin screen | [Section 4.7](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-bid-rigging.html#sec-bidrig-margin) |
| Do the same firms bid higher when no outsider competes? | Inside and outside comparison | [Section 4.8](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-bid-rigging.html#sec-bidrig-inout) |
| Did prices fall when a new firm entered a district? | Bid to estimate ratio, before and after | [Section 4.9](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-bid-rigging.html#sec-bidrig-ratio) |
| Are two competing bidders really one business? | Links in the contractor register | [Section 4.10](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-bid-rigging.html#sec-bidrig-links), [Section 4.15](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-bid-rigging.html#sec-bidrig-phantom) |
| Did two bidders quote identical unusual rates? | Comparing item rates in a bill of quantities | [Section 4.11](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-bid-rigging.html#sec-bidrig-boq) |
| Was competition restricted in a department's tenders? | Process red flags, single bids against similar tenders | [Section 3.3](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-tender-flags.html#sec-tenderflags-notice), [Section 3.4](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-tender-flags.html#sec-tenderflags-single) |
| Were works split to avoid an open tender? | Bunching below the limit, tenders issued together | [Section 3.5](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-tender-flags.html#sec-tenderflags-split) |
| Does one firm win most of a department's contracts? | Winner's share of the buyer's contracts | [Section 3.6](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-tender-flags.html#sec-tenderflags-share) |
| Were calls cancelled until a particular firm won? | Re-tendering against the first call's lowest bidder | [Section 3.7](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-tender-flags.html#sec-tenderflags-after) |
| Were contracts won low and raised later by variations? | Award and final value against the estimate | [Section 3.10](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-tender-flags.html#sec-tenderflags-variation) |
| Which tenders, departments and firms should be examined first? | A simple corruption risk index | [Section 3.8](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21c-tender-flags.html#sec-tenderflags-cri) |
| Do the bids within a large tender look arranged? | Shape screens, for tenders with four or more bids | [Section 5.2](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21d-bid-shapes.html#sec-bidshape-screens) |
| Can a cartel be seen when genuine outsiders also bid? | Screens on subgroups of three or four bids | [Section 5.4](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21d-bid-shapes.html#sec-bidshape-subgroups) |
| Can past proved cases train a model to rank tenders? | Random forest on screens, with its false alarms and misses | [Section 5.5](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21d-bid-shapes.html#sec-bidshape-forest), [Section 5.7](https://anilyayavar.github.io/book2/21d-bid-shapes.html#sec-bidshape-ranking) |
| Were tenders open on the portal for the required number of days? | Web pages, dates | @sec-web-days |
| Does the tender register agree with what the portal published? | Web pages, joins | @sec-web-days, @sec-web-links |
| Were payments made to firms on a published debarred list? | Web pages, fuzzy matching | @sec-web-debarred |
| How do I keep data taken from a website as audit evidence? | Dated copies and a log | @sec-web-evidence |
| Do tender specifications name a brand? | Text analytics | @sec-text-brands |
| Is an employee linked to a vendor through a bank account, mobile number or address? | Networks | @sec-net-empvendor |
| Do different vendors work from the same place? | Geocoding | @sec-geocode-samevendor |
| Were lead charges claimed for longer distances than the real ones? | Geocoding | @sec-geocode-lead |
| Was the purchase process followed, step by step? | Process mining | @sec-process-traces, @sec-process-rules |
| Did the same person approve and pay? | Segregation of duties | @sec-process-sod |
| Which steps of a process took too long? | Process mining | @sec-process-time |

| Were entries made on holidays or late at night? | Dates and times | @sec-lubri-audit, @sec-lubri-hours |

| How do I make a district table safe to publish? | Small-cell suppression | @sec-privacy-table |
| How do I send a data file safely by email or pen drive? | Encryption with a passphrase | @sec-privacy-encrypt |
| How can a department send identifiers that only the auditor can read? | Encryption with a pair of keys | @sec-privacy-keys, @sec-privacy-keyuse |

## Reporting {.unnumbered}

| Audit question | Technique | Where |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------|
| How do I make a chart fit for an audit report? | ggplot2 | @sec-ggplot2-audit |
| How do I produce a report for every district from one template? | Parameterised Quarto reports | @sec-reports-quarto, @sec-reports-loop |
| How do I give the field party Excel working papers? | Working papers | @sec-reports-excel |
| How should I organise the files of an audit project? | Project structure | @sec-reports-project |

:::

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var box = document.getElementById("finder-filter");
  var count = document.getElementById("finder-count");
  var root = document.getElementById("finder");
  if (!box || !root) return;
  var rows = root.querySelectorAll("tbody tr");
  function apply() {
    var q = box.value.trim().toLowerCase();
    var shown = 0;
    rows.forEach(function (r) {
      var hit = !q || r.textContent.toLowerCase().indexOf(q) !== -1;
      r.style.display = hit ? "" : "none";
      if (hit) shown++;
    });
    root.querySelectorAll("section").forEach(function (s) {
      var any = Array.prototype.some.call(s.querySelectorAll("tbody tr"),
        function (r) { return r.style.display !== "none"; });
      s.style.display = any ? "" : "none";
    });
    count.textContent = q ? shown + " of " + rows.length + " questions" : "";
  }
  box.addEventListener("input", apply);
})();
</script>
```
